text: Items and metrics that produce data we cannot use as planned. The provider-reported prompt_tokens field is not comparable across endpoints: the same 200 prompts are counted as 49 tokens on average by CoreWeave and Cloudflare, 57 by Anthropic, 68 by Groq and by llama.cpp. The providers apply different chat templates and tokenizers, so prompt-token counts are reported but cost is compared only through the provider's own billed cost per request. The local power figures are not comparable either: powermetrics on the Mac reports CPU and GPU package power (19 W under load), nvidia-smi on the T4 reports the card alone (66 W), and neither sees the rest of the machine; we therefore treat energy as a secondary input and show in the cost model that it changes cost per 1,000 requests by less than 1 percent at every volume. The concurrency-4 level on the Mac produces a number that is correct but misleading on its own: aggregate throughput rises only from 43 to 52 tokens/s between concurrency 1 and 4 while per-request speed falls from 48 to 14 tokens/s, and then jumps to 139 tokens/s at concurrency 16. This is a property of the Metal backend of llama.cpp at small batch sizes, reproduced in all three repeats of both Mac runs and absent on the T4 (26, 59, 154 tokens/s), so the three-level design cannot be read as a smooth curve for the Mac.

Where runs behaved differently from the protocol's assumptions. The two cheapest fp8 endpoints, DeepInfra and Novita, refused every request with HTTP 429 for about half an hour at 01:34 Astana time (US evening); DeepInfra then accepted requests at 04:10, refused almost everything again from 04:35, and in the 05:14 rerun still dropped 20 percent of all requests (46 to 68 percent at concurrency 4, 0 percent at concurrency 16), so 'the cheapest provider' is available only at some hours and the failure rate depends on the hour more than on the concurrency; Cloudflare was added as a second fp8 provider, and all hosted conditions now carry the time of day of their runs in the meta line. The rate limiting we expected from Groq never appeared: 1,800 main requests at concurrency up to 16 all succeeded, while CoreWeave, which we expected to be stable, dropped 14 connections in one repeat. The Colab L4 runtime we planned was not available and the session ran on a free-tier Tesla T4 (confirmed by the Resources panel after the run), which decodes single requests at 26 tokens/s, slower than the Mac, so the rented condition is a weaker machine than the one we described in the protocol. Building llama.cpp on the two-core Colab VM took 54 minutes instead of 8, and the server could not bind port 8080 because Colab occupies it. The pilot set of 50 prompts predicted the main set poorly at concurrency 4 (84 against 52 tokens/s on the Mac); our first explanation, GUI load from the open Chrome tab, was wrong, because the idle rerun gave the same 51 tokens/s, so the difference comes from the answer-length mix of the two prompt sets.

What we changed, with dates. 23.10.2026 01:36: Cloudflare added as a second fp8 provider. 02:00: prices moved to current US list prices in USD with sources, and a second attribution scenario (25 percent of hardware cost) added. 02:10: a cost-only 'budget inference box' configuration added that reuses the PC measurements. 02:15: the rented-GPU condition moved from RunPod to a public Colab notebook. 02:45: a Q8_0 condition added on the Mac to test quantization. 03:10: Colab server port changed to 8090. 03:12: the first Mac main run kept as a separate 'loaded machine' observation and the protocol repeated on an idle machine. 04:12: DeepInfra main and pilot protocols run when the endpoint became available. None of these changes touched the prompt sets, the seed, the decoding parameters, the concurrency levels or the answer parser, so every run remains comparable with every other.

What will change and what will stay fixed. The PC condition will be run by the team with the identical scripts and the same model file (checksum verified) and nothing else will be re-run; DeepInfra's main run happened at a different hour from the other hosted runs and with a 20 percent failure rate; we will state the hours and the failure rate rather than re-run everything at one time, because the instability is itself the operational finding the RQ needs. We will keep the 100-item quality test even though its confidence interval is wide, because changing it would make the pre-registered ER4, ER6 and ER7 untestable; Assignment 4 will report the interval, not only the point estimate. We will keep max_tokens at 256 although 12 percent of the throughput answers are cut at that limit, because the cut is identical in every condition and lifting it would change the token mix behind every cost figure. We will not add the Novita endpoint or a second Anthropic model: the design already has two fp8, one bf16, one Groq and one closed-weight hosted condition, and adding more would not change the answer to the RQ, which the pilot data already points to: below 100,000 requests per day a dedicated consumer machine does not beat the cheapest hosted price of the same model, and the break-even exists only if the machine's cost is mostly attributed to something else.
